item.title: Quasi-stationary solutions of the dP$_\text{I}$ equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study real quasi-stationary solutions of the discrete Painlev\'e-I equation (dP$_\text{I}$) which defines a reduction of the Volterra lattice and the B\"acklund transformations for the Painlev\'e-IV equation (P$_\text{IV}$). It is shown that the quasi-stationary asymptotics for large $|n|$ is preserved under the evolution of the solution with respect to the parameter $t$ governed by P$_\text{IV}$ and, conversely, the quasi-stationary asymptotics for large $|t|$ is preserved under the evolution with respect to $n$ governed by dP$_\text{I}$. This makes it possible to speak of a common quasi-stationary surface and, in the case of uniform asymptotics, of common quasi-stationary solutions for these equations. Examples (exact and numerical) are given of solutions demonstrating quasi-stationary and pole behavior in different regions of the $(n,t)$-plane. The existence of global quasi-stationary solutions is shown numerically. A uniformly valid self-similar asymptotics is constructed in the transition zone between the branches of the quasi-stationary curve, related to Hastings--McLeod type solutions of the Painlev\'e-II equation (P$_\text{II}$).
item.dc:creator: V. E. Adler, B. I. Suleimanov

item.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.
item.dc:creator: Jinbing Chen, Colin Grant, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

item.title: Algebraic dark solitons versus rogue waves in the massive Thirring model
item.description: arXiv:2611.27045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the existence of algebraically decaying solitary waves on the nonzero wave background in the massive Thirring model (MTM) in laboratory coordinates. We find the precise condition of the spectral stability and instability of the nonzero wave background. In the case of instability, we distinguish modulational, side-band, and full-band instabilities and show that the rogue wave exists if and only if the nonzero wave background is modulationally unstable. For the other unstable cases and in the case of stability, we show that there exist exactly two algebraic dark solitons which correspond to the end points in the admissible range of the wave speed for the dark soliton propagation.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Zhao, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

item.title: Direct linearization, Cauchy matrix and Sato Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2608.24538v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fu and Nijhoff's direct linearization scheme for the KP hierarchy employs a system of evolution equations of an infinite matrix U. Part of the matrix elements of U can be identified with affine coordinates of the top cell of the Sato Grassmannian. The evolution equations of these matrix elements are identical to the KP hierarchy realized as a dynamical system on the Sato Grassmannian. The system of evolution equations of U itself can be extended by the so called negative flows, and the extended system turns out to be equivalent to the two-component KP hierarchy. The Cauchy matrix approach to the KP hierarchy can be re-interpreted in this geometric perspective. This geometric interpretation of the direct linearization scheme persists to be useful for a multi-component generalization. The AKNS and anti-self-dual Yang-Mills hierarchies fall into this scheme. Multi-component Sato Grassmannians show up therein as the relevant geometric structure.
item.dc:creator: Kanehisa Takasaki
